newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil convicts actor ex-wife in soap opera murder.
newsitem.headline: Brazil convicts actor ex-wife in soap opera murder.

text.p: The ex-wife of a TV soap opera actor accused of murdering his screen lover was convicted Friday, concluding a sensational murder case that fascinated Brazilians for five years.
After all-night deliberations and summing up, a jury of four women and three men found 23-year-old Paula Thomaz guilty of the 1992 murder of soap opera star Daniela Perez.

Judge Jose Geraldo Antonio sentenced Thomaz to 19 years in jail, describing her as "violent, perverse and cowardly." He subsequently lowered the sentence to 18 years and six months because Thomaz was under 21 years of age at the time of the crime.
Thomaz and her ex-husband, male-stripper-turned-TV-star Guilherme de Padua, 27, were accused jointly of murdering Perez. He was convicted and sentenced to 19 years in jail in January.
Both have already served four years of their sentences while awaiting trial.
Thomaz maintained throughout that she was innocent and out shopping by herself at the time of the crime.

The shocking murder of 22-year-old Perez, who was found dead on a Rio roadside with 16 stab wounds, made headlines around the world and managed to eclipse the historic resignation of former President Fernando Collor.
Padua, who originally confessed to the crime, said Perez had been hounding him to have sex with her. But later, after his divorce from Thomaz, he accused his ex-wife.
During his testimony, Padua said Thomaz carried out the murder in a fit of jealousy, stabbing Perez at least 15 times with a pair of scissors.
He said he had an affair with Perez because her mother, Gloria, was the script writer for the soap opera in which he was co-starring with Perez and it was in his interests to keep on her good side.

The case became Brazil's equivalent to the O.J. Simpson trial in the United States. It dragged on for almost five years, littered with interviews by the defendants from behind bars, conflicting testimony from limelight-seeking witnesses and angry calls for justice from the victim's family.

Millions of Brazilian soap opera fans have watched its twists and turns as closely as the soap opera, "De Corpo e Alma" (Of Body and Soul), in which Padua rocketed to fame as the brooding lover of sexy Yasmin, played by Perez.
